abstract_summary: Large language model (LLM) agents that serve users across many sessions must choose, for every request, the few stored memories that enter a limited context window. This choice largely decides whether the agent answers correctly, and it runs on every request at Web scale. This selection faces three challenges: a lar...

cascades and
factorizes accuracy into the completeness that each stage controls.
Guided by it, we proposeAgentMemRec, which adapts candidate
generation, learning to rank and slate construction from recom-
mender systems and selects memories without any LLM call. On
multi-session questions of LongMemEval,AgentMemRecoutper-
forms memory and context-selection methods, including A-Mem,
HippoRAG 2, DynamicRAG and T-Mem, by 10 to 31 points of ac-
curacy. It matches an LLM reranker that makes 64 calls per query
at 3.2 times lower serving cost, and on LoCoMo it outperforms
Mem0 and Zep without any LLM call at write time. The factoriza-
tion attributes the gains to slates that more often hold all of the
evidence, so recommender-system design offers an effective and
efficient foundation for the long-term memory of LLM agents.

evidence.excerpt:
When evidence units are independent, the set-level objective re-
duces to ranking units by their probability of being evidence. The
ranker therefore learns item relevance from gold labels, and with
𝐿=0it uses cheap features, as recommender cascades do.Agent-
MemRecuses a LightGBM model [20] trained with the LambdaRank
objective [4, 41]. Each (question, pooled turn) pair has ten features.
Five are cheap relevance signals: the bge-m3 cosine, the logarithms
of the global dense and BM25 ranks, the position in the fused pool
and the bge-reranker-v2-m3 cross-encoder score. Five describe the
turn: whether its role is user, its relative position in its session,
the logarithms of its age in days and of its length, and the spaCy
keys it shares with the question. The labels are the gold annota-
tions of the 152 development questions, with pools from both their
LongMemEval-S and LongMemEval-M

The slate stage fills the budget𝐵 from the ranked pool. It walks the
pool in rank order and adds each turn whose rendered cost still fits.
The rendered cost of a turn is the increase in the token count of the
rendered slate when the turn is added, including its session header
if no earlier turn of that session was selected. A turn that does
not fit is skipped, and the walk continues. The rendering groups
the selected turns by session, orders sessions by date and uses the
official LongMemEval history format (Appendix A). The budget
is fixed at 𝐵= 2,700tokens, a value set in our first experiment
before any system was compared, and the evaluation perturbs it
to 2,400 to 2,700. There is no per-question cutoff, because the fill
contains every prefix that fits, so a cutoff can only help where a
lower-ranked turn lowers the value of the slate. On the ranking of

Benchmarks and splits.Like most memory papers, we evaluate on
LongMemEval-S [40] and LoCoMo [26]. LongMemEval-S (cleaned
release) has 500 questions over histories of about 50 sessions and
100k tokens. LongMemEval-M shares its questions over histories
of about 500 sessions and 1.5M tokens, and serves as a harder third
setting. We exclude the 30 questions of the unanswerable type and
compute𝜅 over the other 470. A split fixed before any method run
assigns 152 of the 500 questions of both variants to development
and 348 to test, of which 328 are answerable. The primary stratum
is𝜅≥ 2on test, with 𝑛= 209, and we also report 𝜅≥ 3(49 test
questions). Label-only and oracle measurements have no learned
component and use all 300 questions with𝜅≥ 2. LoCoMo has 1,540
scored questions in 10 conversations. As the field does, we report
all of them, and we add paired comparisons on test conversations

Answering and judging.On LongMemEval, two answering mod-
els read every slate: Qwen3-32B [43] with FP8 weights under vLLM,
and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash [ 13] through one pinned FP8 provider.
Both decode at temperature 0 with reasoning disabled and the of-
ficial step-by-step answer prompt of LongMemEval. Final labels

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline accuracy is measured on held-out test splits with independent answering models and external LLM judges, with 97.3% agreement between GPT-4o and Qwen3-32B judges.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Held-out test question-answering accuracy judged by GPT-4o and Qwen3-32B over answers from Qwen3-32B, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and GPT-4o-mini.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: LightGBM LambdaRank trained on gold turn annotations from the 152 development questions, or distilled from Qwen3-8B offline scores.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims that AgentMemRec outperforms turn-level context selectors and LLM-built memories by 10 to 33 points while matching a 64-call LLM reranker at 3.2x lower latency and cost are supported by comprehensive tables, calibrations across GPT-4o and Qwen judges, and error/filler analyses.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluations are rigorous across LongMemEval-S, LongMemEval-M, and LoCoMo, accounting for inference non-determinism via multi-budget decoding, paired bootstrap statistical tests, and explicit factorizations separating candidate recall, ranking completeness, and complete slate rewards.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline QA accuracy is validated on held-out test instances with independent answering models and external LLM judges, showing strong agreement (97.3% between GPT-4o and Qwen3-32B judges) across multiple decodes.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: End-to-end downstream question-answering accuracy evaluated on held-out test splits using GPT-4o and Qwen3-32B judges across answer generations from Qwen3-32B, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and GPT-4o-mini.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: LightGBM LambdaRank trained on pairwise gold turn annotations from the 152 development questions (or distilled from Qwen3-8B offline scores).

primary.limitations: The authors identify degradation on instances requiring evidence across three or more sessions (kappa >= 3), sensitivity to near-miss filler distractors in complete slates, and performance variations across target answering models.
primary.method_assessment: The method is clearly specified: a 128-candidate pool formed from BM25 and bge-m3 dense embeddings via reciprocal rank fusion, scored with a 10-feature LightGBM LambdaRank model trained on development split gold annotations, followed by greedy budget filling without per-query cutoffs.
primary.quality_rationale: The work provides a sound theoretical formulation uniting memory architectures into a recommender cascade and demonstrates strong empirical gains using zero-LLM-call ranking, supported by thorough baseline reproductions, cost measurements, and independent evaluation controls.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper formalizes long-term LLM agent memory selection as budgeted slate recommendation and presents AgentMemRec, a non-LLM cascade using reciprocal rank fusion over lexical/dense channels, LightGBM LambdaRank over ten inexpensive features, and budget filling.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The work provides a sound theoretical formulation uniting memory architectures into a recommender cascade and demonstrates strong empirical gains using zero-LLM-call ranking, supported by thorough baseline reproductions, cost measurements, and independent evaluation controls.
